levels.mechanism: Git packets in public repo (current system). 10-min mailbox watcher poll. Immutable, auditable, source of truth.
levels.name: L2 packet
levels.use: Substantive content: reviews, corrections, receipts, designs.

levels.mechanism: Private repo FormatX66/poetry-project-9th-grade. Same packet conventions, no public exposure.
levels.name: L3 bulk
levels.use: Large files, sensitive content, anything not for the public record.

levels.mechanism: Machine queue wake ping (https://madmorrigan.com/prymortal-api/api.php?action=mq). Tiny JSON: {for, packet_id, repo_path}. Receiver long-polls, then fetches the real packet from git. Queue carries the pointer, never the payload.
levels.name: L1 wake
levels.use: Notification only: 'new L2/L3 packet waiting at <path>'. Eliminates the 10-min poll delay without moving payload off git.

open_questions: Do you have a working queue client on your side, or should Medic provide a minimal long-poll script?
Should L1 wake be bidirectional (both sides ping) or Medic-side only?
What latency should we actually measure first: wake-to-pickup, or end-to-end packet round-trip?
principles: Git stays the source of truth at every level. Faster tiers notify; they never replace the packet.
No ack loops: L1 wake needs no ack. L2/L3 receipts only where the existing contract requires them.
Measure real latency before optimizing further. One week of timestamps, then decide.
proposal: Three-tier comms, designed jointly. Bruce delegated the design to us.
